title: How Far Ahead of Departure a Cabin Move Is Bought on the Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
A cabin move bought well ahead of the outbound departure carries a smaller share forward than one bought close to it, provided the Air Ticket Fare Brands brand held releases its seat map before departure at all.

## 1. The share carried forward

1.1 Where the outbound departs more than 30 days from today and the fare brand releases its seat map before departure, the early share is carried forward: 0.9, being 90 percent.

1.2 Where the outbound departs more than 7 days from today but not more than 30, and the fare brand releases its seat map before departure, the standard share is carried forward: 1, the whole of the figure.

1.3 In every other case no such treatment applies to the share.

A brand releases its seat map before departure when the release point scheduled for it stands above 0 hours before departure. The days are counted from today to the outbound departure date, and each test is on "more than": a departure exactly 30 days away does not exceed 30, and one exactly 7 days away does not exceed 7.

## 2. Boundary readings, on hypothetical dates

On a brand whose seat map is released before departure: an outbound 31 days away exceeds 30, so 0.9 is carried forward. An outbound exactly 30 days away does not exceed 30 but does exceed 7, so the whole of the figure is carried forward. An outbound 8 days away likewise carries the whole of it forward. An outbound exactly 7 days away exceeds neither test, and no such treatment applies.

On a brand whose seat map release point stands at 0 hours, neither of the first two rows can hold however far off the outbound stands.
